open_a.text: Good morning, I'm Anders Fjell, and this is Nordic Crypto. Here are the week's biggest stories from the Nordic crypto world.
bounds: Good morning, I'm Anders Fjell, and this is Nordic Crypto.

open_b.text: This week: Norway's minister says crypto mining in data centres is not widespread. Sweden's central bank looks at an e-krona. And Apple and BlackRock in the bitcoin headlines.
bounds: This week: Norway's minister says crypto mining in data centres is not widespread.
Sweden's central bank looks at an e-krona.
And Apple and BlackRock in the bitcoin headlines.

s1.text: Norway's digitalisation minister, Torgeir Micaelsen, told the Storting in a written answer that crypto mining in data centres is not widespread. The register shows mining at eight of 113 data centres. The government is assessing a temporary, limited ban, subject to EEA law. Ságat reported the answer.

s2.text: TV 2 reports that five people are on trial in Oslo District Court over a home robbery in which the robbers demanded two million dollars in crypto.

s2.text: One posed as a food courier. The five are charged, and have not been convicted.

s3.text: In Sweden, Riksbank deputy governor Per Jansson told Reuters that Sweden should prepare for a possible e-krona, pointing to the digital euro and stablecoins.
bounds: In Sweden, Riksbank deputy governor Per Jansson told Reuters that Sweden should prepare for a possible e-krona, pointing to the digital euro and stablecoins.

s3.text: No decision has been taken. Hurbra reported the interview.

s4.text: Dagens Nyheter reports on criticism after Israel's prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu suggested crypto could help get around possible sanctions. The Bank of Israel replied that cryptocurrencies cannot serve that purpose.

s5.text: Realtid reports that Apple has asked a US court to dismiss a lawsuit from three investors who say they lost one point eight million dollars through a fake bitcoin wallet app in the App Store.

s5.text: Apple says it cannot be held responsible for outside fraudsters.

s6.text: And BlackRock has filed for a bitcoin fund designed to limit losses, ticker P-BIT, Kryptovalutaguiden reports. The filing is incomplete, and the shares may not be sold until it becomes effective.

s7.text: Finally, the Bitcoin Ordinals art project Tiny Vikings planned to unveil what it calls the world's largest Tiny Viking in Marfa, Texas, on the 22nd of October, according to its event page.
